terms.gloss: wise; (as a noun) a wise man
terms.comment: Wise in judgement and in living; sapiēns alone is “the wise man” of the philosophers. Wisdom is sapientia, wisely sapienter (Traupman 133: Sapienter dēcrēvistī).

evidence: Cic. Lael. 6: prūdēns in jūre cīvīlī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From prōvidēns: wise in practical matters, far-sighted, and also “skilled in” (with the genitive). Unwise is imprūdēns, which also means “without meaning to”.

phrases.english: A word to the wise is enough.
The wise man will rule his mind; the fool will be its slave.

phrases.latin: Ex vitiō alius sapiēns ēmendat suum.
phrases.english: The wise man mends his own fault from another’s.
